common_mistakes.mistake: Isp walks into Pac on STEADY or Pac leaves before RESCUE.
common_mistakes.consequence: Pac can be pushed off the pad; the bridge loses stabilization and Isp landing gate closes. Continued supported bridge occupancy can collapse it and cause a lethal fall.
common_mistakes.recovery: If nobody fell, Pac reoccupies STEADY, which immediately reactivates/stabilizes the bridge and resets timers. A slime fall kills the shared room state; retry repeats pad placement and crossing.

confidence_reason: Current source, retained idle PNGs and accepted ordinary-input browser endpoint establish mechanics and one feasible route. Difficulty is an expert estimate; human discovery, errors, recovery behavior, enjoyment and physical keyboard comfort remain unmeasured.

confirmed: Support/rescue with reversed roles, meaningful slime exposure, and one ordered handoff are confirmed. The source gives no basis to treat visible repeated movement as extra reasoning.
missed_mechanics: STEADY simultaneously opens Isp landing and removes collapse; RESCUE permanently replaces it and opens Pac finish. Heroes can push one another off the supporting pad, making an over-partner jump useful. Boomerang has no rescue interruption binding here.
incorrect_inferences: First-pass execution1 assumed the level bridge needed only horizontal travel; it missed the physical partner obstruction and accepted over-partner jump. It correctly left START: STEADY persistence unknown rather than calling the bridge permanently safe.
changed_judgments: execution 1 -> 2: production hero collision/pushing and the accepted early Isp jump establish a controlled movement/placement demand that the idle broad bridge obscured. The later Pac jump is viable attack handling, not proof of a universally mandatory jump.
timing null -> 1: active support eliminates collapse timing; only a maintained handoff and forgiving far-bank interference remain, rather than an unverified race across a disappearing bridge.
recovery_cost null -> 2: source confirms lethal slime resets both-room setup, while reoccupying STEADY can rescue a nonfatal support loss; this replaces the idle recovery unknown.
Remaining scores retained; source makes consequences known without creating extra causal dependencies. Control friction remains null.
unresolved: No human novice/paired-keyboard observation; prior exposure offers learning rather than proving mastery.
Common-mistake recovery descriptions are source-derived possibilities, not witnessed player errors.

single_operator_note: One operator must manage both control sets and preserve one hero's support position while moving the other. This extra input-management demand is outside the two-human baseline.
